triggeringTask: Compress Phase 1 of plans/docs-quality-metrics-gap.plans.md
gap: When constructing multi-line file content via python -c @"..."@ or inline Node.js, PowerShell double-quoted here-strings interpret backtick-n (`n) as newline escapes. This caused backtick-quoted commands like `npm` to be mangled (e.g., `npm` became newline + pm) and corrupted generated Markdown files.
resolution: Switch to writing a temporary .mjs script file with the literal content and executing it with node, avoiding PowerShell here-string escaping entirely.
confirmation: Resolution verified by byte-level inspection; final files contain correct triple backticks and inline backtick quoting.
resumeAction: For Markdown writes with backticks, prefer file-based script execution over inline here-strings.

gap:
Two orchestration-level gaps were found while amending the Step 14J packet at contract level. (1) The consolidated `slice-advancement` gate runs exactly four TRIVIAL sub-gates (plan-sync, step-packet, plan-slice-quality, plan-command-lint) plus three FULL gates (shared-validation, code-coverage, specialist-review) - it does NOT include `convergence-tracker`. Yet `convergence-tracker` is the gate that reads the `fix-loop: <slice-id> iteration <n> status=<failed|passed>` markers under `## Latest validation evidence`, so a fix-loop cycle can be fully patched and re-gated with `slice-advancement` reporting 4/4 PASS while the tracker has never observed the cycle at all. (2) The `step-packet` gate captures the `## Latest validation evidence` section with the regex /^## Latest validation evidence\s*?
([\s\S]*?)(?=?
## |$)/m - the `m` flag makes the lazy `(?=?

The practical consequence: the authoring instance cannot self-record a verdict either way, which is consistent with the author/verify loop-ownership rule, but the truncation is a gate-side defect that should not be relied upon as a safety net.
resolution: Appended the fix-loop markers for the amended slices by hand at the `<!-- EVIDENCE-APPEND-POINT -->` marker inside `## Latest validation evidence`, outside any code fence and at the start of a line in the exact format `fix-loop: <slice-id> iteration <n> status=<failed|passed>`. confirmation: Learning event appended; convergence-tracker re-run confirms the fix-loop markers are counted; slice-advancement re-run for all five Step 14J slices passes 4/4 TRIVIAL sub-gates each.
resumeAction: A future orchestration pass should either add `convergence-tracker` to the `slice-advancement` composite (or to a documented TRIVIAL/FULL set that includes it), and should fix the `step-packet` green-light capture regex by removing the `m` flag (or by anchoring the terminator with a non-multiline lookahead) so both gates read the same evidence section. Until then, plan authors must append fix-loop markers manually and must not treat the `step-packet` green-light warning as an authoritative readiness signal.

description: A determinism assertion is only acceptable if it is mutation-proven or hand-computed; re-deriving with production code is a tautology
evidence: A Tier-3 determinism-reviewer flagged that the reserved-bleacher-slot assertion re-derived the expected value with the SAME algorithm production uses, so it could never fail. A second attempt was also tautological: a tripwire that re-derived the ring band sizes LOCALLY (from the same 0.25 split as production) did not fail under a production mutation of that split to 0.3. Remedy now in the repo: the tripwire was rewritten to READ THE BAND SIZES BACK FROM THE PRODUCTION EMISSION (examples/neatRacing/track/right-world.builder.test.ts:1539 'derives the reachable ring configuration from the track generator' - 'the inner/outer band sizes are read back from the emitted props, not re-derived here'), after which the same mutation failed the test.

Apply this rule to every new contract in Step 14J and require the reviewer to name the falsification method before accepting an assertion.

description: ts.readConfigFile(path) called WITHOUT the second ts.sys.readFile argument silently returns an undefined config, so ts.parseJsonConfigFileContent(...) yields EMPTY compiler options; a verification matrix built on those empty options matches NOTHING, even for files that are byte-identical under the correct options. Always pass the readFile callback, and prove any JSDoc/comment-only documentation pass behaviour-neutral with TWO independent, comment-insensitive TypeScript compiler-API fingerprints: (1) the SHA-256 of ts.transpileModule(src, { removeComments: true, compilerOptions: <repo tsconfig options> }).outputText, and (2) the raw character length of ts.createPrinter({ removeComments: true }).printFile(sf) - each PROVEN comment-insensitive first, by injecting a JSDoc block and a plain line comment into a copy and confirming the fingerprint does not move. Measure 2 is stronger than measure 1 because the printer AST print normalises string-literal quote style, which the emitter preserves.
evidence: During the Step 14K docs-quality closure pass (2026-10-23) the four-source-file behaviour-verification matrix was first run with ts.readConfigFile(path) (no readFile argument), which returned an undefined config; ts.parseJsonConfigFileContent then produced EMPTY compiler options, and the resulting transpile digest matched NO recorded pre-edit digest for ANY of the four changed source files, including the two that were byte-identical under the correct options. Had that matrix been trusted, the closure would have wrongly reported that all four changed source files had changed behaviour. The matrix was invalidated and re-run with the correct ts.readConfigFile(path, ts.sys.readFile) options, after which two of the four files reproduced their recorded pre-edit digests EXACTLY, confirming the documentation-only pass was behaviour-neutral. Both fingerprints were each proven comment-insensitive (a JSDoc block and a plain line comment injected into a copy; the fingerprint did not move) before being trusted.
followup_action: Always call ts.readConfigFile(path, ts.sys.readFile) and ASSERT the parsed config options are non-empty before using them; an empty or undefined options object is the signature of the missing readFile callback, and a fingerprint matrix that matches nothing is a defect in the matrix, never evidence of behaviour change. For any JSDoc/comment-only edit, use the two independent comment-insensitive compiler-API fingerprints (removeComments:true transpile SHA-256 plus removeComments:true printer printFile character length), prove each is comment-insensitive by comment injection before trusting it, prefer the printer length as the stronger measure because the emitter preserves string-literal quote style while the printer AST normalises it, and never conclude behaviour changed from a single fingerprint - require agreement of two independent measures plus exact reproduction of the pre-edit digest for files that are unchanged.

description: Three reusable Puppeteer/WebGL harness gaps plus one latent quadratic fixture hot spot were measured while repairing the visible-foreground drift smoke fixture, and together they make a browser-validation slice fail for reasons that live in the HARNESS rather than in the code under test, or hang with a message that points at the wrong cause: (1) page.setContent() does NOT re-run page.evaluateOnNewDocument() hooks, so the WebGL interception never installs and the harness reports 'no data captured' instead of 'the hook did not install' - a silent false-negative generator; (2) the default Puppeteer protocolTimeout of 180 s is shorter than a legitimately long fixture run and its failure text ('Runtime.callFunctionOn timed out') is indistinguishable from a hung page, when the real cause was a busy renderer main thread; (3) a backgrounded or occluded window throttles requestAnimationFrame, so the fixture can silently never progress and the run only advances when the window is genuinely visible AND in the foreground; and (4) the fixture itself carried an O(greenPoints x roadPoints) brute-force nearest-road scan that was unreachable behind the earlier staleness failure and only became reachable after the repair, where it blocked the renderer main thread for minutes. The consequence is that a browser smoke can be declared broken (or hung) for harness reasons, and a fixture that was previously 'not reached' can hide a quadratic main-thread hot spot.
evidence: (1) setContent vs evaluateOnNewDocument: the WebGL interception is installed through page.evaluateOnNewDocument(...); under page.setContent(html) the hook NEVER ran - the probe proved it because the expected injected globals __p1ctxCount and __p1frames were ABSENT from the page context, the fixture captured no buffer upload at all and every probe reported 'failed to capture the VBO'; the identical page content served through page.goto(url) DID run the hook and the injection keys appeared. (2) protocolTimeout: the first visible-window run died with 'Runtime.callFunctionOn timed out' (a 180 s waitForFunction timeout) which looks exactly like a hung page, but the renderer main thread was merely busy (see (4)); protocolTimeout: 900000 is required for this fixture class. (3) foreground requirements: the render only advanced when the window was genuinely visible AND in the foreground; the working combination on this host was page.goto() (not setContent), the Chrome flags --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows --disable-renderer-backgrounding --disable-background-timer-throttling --disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion, page.bringToFront(), and a Win32 foreground-activation helper (SetForegroundWindow / BringWindowToTop / ShowWindow applied to the Chrome window whose command line contains the test --user-data-dir), applied repeatedly during the run; a separate --user-data-dir outside the repo is required while the developer's own Chrome is running; and a page.setContent() page must receive the fixture CSS or the canvas is 0x0 and nothing renders. (4) the O(n^2) fixture hot spot: the fixture measured the distance from every coloured track vertex to the nearest road point with a brute-force O(greenPoints x roadPoints) scan over 603,300 road points; measured 147 ms for 201 green points, i.e. an extrapolated ~170 s for the three band means, which is what blocked the renderer main thread in (2); the repair replaced it with an EXACT uniform-grid nearest-road search (4 m cells, expanding ring, a proven-exact termination bound plus an exhaustive fallback) whose result is IDENTICAL - 300 sampled green points, 0 mismatches against the brute force, maxDiff 0 - at ~1,100 ms instead of ~170 s. Also measured: the same fixture class silently dropped undefined-valued check keys through JSON.stringify, which is why ten road-edge checks were invisible in the serialized result of the earlier NOT OK verdict; and the repaired fixture now reports window.p1TurnDriftGreenSmokeResult.passed === true with all 31 checks true, reproduced across TWO captured runs (9,831 ms and 10,506 ms) in a NON-HEADLESS visible foreground Chrome 155.0.8059.85 window with 0 fixture console errors.
followup_action: (a) DONE inside this slice (fixture-only, one file: docs/browser-tests/scenarios/p1-turn-drift-green-smoke.html): the O(n^2) nearest-road scan is replaced by the exact uniform-grid search (ROAD_GRID_CELL_M = 4, expanding ring, proven-exact termination bound, exhaustive fallback) with IDENTICAL results at ~1,100 ms instead of ~170 s; the singlePlanePaint measurement is now taken on the paint plane only (PAINT_Y_THRESHOLD) so the 37,452-vertex ground slab at y = -0.5 is no longer counted as paint; the three enumerated staleness defects (track program marker, 7-float track VBO stride, wheel VBO selection by measured identity) are closed; and the fixture now reports passed === true with all 31 checks true in a visible foreground window (two captured runs, 9,831 ms and 10,506 ms, Chrome 155.0.8059.85, 0 console errors). NO harness-level fix landed - the remediation in (b) is still open. (b) REMAINING for agent-maintenance-coordinator with browser-harness-specialist and browser-ui-specialist: land ONE reusable visible-foreground smoke harness contract in .github/skills/browser-testing-harness/SKILL.md and the browser-harness-specialist agent that states: (i) navigate with page.goto(url) and NEVER page.setContent() when the scenario depends on a page.evaluateOnNewDocument(...) injection, AND assert the injected globals (__p1ctxCount / __p1frames) are present BEFORE consuming capture data, so a missing hook is reported as 'the hook did not install' and never as 'no data captured'; (ii) an explicit long protocolTimeout (900000 ms) for this fixture class, with the timeout error path stating 'the renderer main thread may be busy - distinguish it from a hang' and, on a protocol timeout, re-checking main-thread liveness before reporting a hang; (iii) the anti-throttling launch contract - the four Chrome flags --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows --disable-renderer-backgrounding --disable-background-timer-throttling --disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion, page.bringToFront(), a Win32 foreground-activation helper (SetForegroundWindow / BringWindowToTop / ShowWindow on the Chrome window whose command line contains the test --user-data-dir) applied repeatedly during the run, a separate --user-data-dir outside the repo while the developer's own Chrome is running, and the fixture CSS delivered to any setContent page so the canvas is not 0x0; (iv) a fixture-level serialization rule that a check with an undefined value is emitted explicitly (e.g. null plus a named reason) instead of being dropped by JSON.stringify, so missing checks cannot hide behind a shorter result object. (c) REMAINING for 04-implementing / 05-green-testing: before any browser smoke is trusted as green, re-profile the fixture for quadratic main-thread hot spots (a fixture that was unreachable behind an earlier failure can hide one) and diagnose a protocol timeout as 'the main thread is busy' before diagnosing it as 'the page is hung'.

description: A DEAD legacy read path inside a browser fixture is a LATENT SILENT-DEGRADATION hazard the moment a field is added to the seam it reads. The 14N W3 fixture's readDriftSeam() USED TO read window.neatRacingDebug.drift FIRST - an identifier written NOWHERE in the repo - so if that old 4-field shape had ever been reintroduced it would have been read INSTEAD of the five-field seam, tick would have been undefined, and the tick budgets would have silently degraded to frame budgets. The reusable rule: when a fixture reads a seam, read it from ONE place, and delete every dead or legacy branch on that read path IN THE SAME STEP that changes the seam's shape (No Deferred Cleanup) - a dead branch is not harmless code, it is a shape-selection branch that nothing exercises and everything depends on.
evidence: THE DEAD PATH (now removed): readDriftSeam() (docs/browser-tests/scenarios/p1-turn-drift-green-smoke.html:1266) used to read window.neatRacingDebug.drift first and only then window.neatRacingDriftState; neatRacingDebug is written NOWHERE in the repo - the plan's own record at plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md:9594 states 'the DEAD legacy seam branch (window.neatRacingDebug.drift, written NOWHERE in the repo) is REMOVED from the fixture's readDriftSeam() in the SAME step that introduced the fifth field - a re-introduced 4-field shape would have been read instead of the five-field seam, tick would have been undefined, and the tick budgets would have silently degraded to frame budgets', and the fixture's own comment block (:1258-1265) carries the same rationale. THE HAZARD CHAIN, all on-disk: (1) the production seam is EXACTLY five fields and is written per frame at examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/browser-entry.ts:980-986 (poseRad, slipAngleRad, speedMps, tickHz and tick = car.tick); (2) the fixture's sampleDriftSeam() (:1283-1307) is undefined-tolerant and yields tick: undefined for a 4-field shape; (3) feelCurrentTick() (:1126-1133) returns null when the seam reports no tick, and its own comment says 'every tick-addressed measurement degrades to a frame count'; (4) observeFeelPhase() (:1407, degraded branch :1483-1491) then completes the phase on a FRAME budget of the tick budget and flags it degraded; (5) the CAPTURE POINT is recorded only when NOT degraded (:1519), so the capture would be MISSING rather than wrong; (6) maxFeelPoseRateDegPerS() (:1664-1691) pairs only frames carrying a numeric, INCREASING tick, so with tick undefined it finds ZERO pairs, and the check driftFeelPoseRateBounded is written as 'poseRate.pairs > 0 && poseRate.maxRate <= DRIFT_FEEL_POSE_RATE_MAX_DEG_PER_S' (:2533-2534) - a NON-VACUITY WITNESS, so the check reports FALSE, never a vacuous pass. HONEST NUANCE (so this event is not misread as 'the fixture would have gone falsely green'): the fixture was NOT a silent-green machine - the degraded flag, the missing-capture guard and the pairs > 0 witness would each have turned the mis-read into a FAILED or MISSING-DATA result. The real cost of the dead branch was MISATTRIBUTION (the symptom reads as 'the tick budgets are broken' or 'the pose-rate check failed', not as 'the fixture read a dead 4-field seam shape') plus the risk that a frame-budget fallback produces plausible-looking phase durations; the same-step removal was still right, because the dead branch was a shape-selection branch no test exercised. THE REMOVAL: the branch is gone and the seam is read from ONE place, still defensively - a missing or throwing seam yields null and never aborts the fixture (:1266-1274).
followup_action: (a) When a browser fixture (or any consumer) reads a named seam, keep exactly ONE read path: any legacy or alternate shape branch is DEAD CODE and must be deleted in the same step that changes the seam's shape, never deferred - a deferred dead branch is a latent shape-selection branch that no test exercises. (b) When a seam gains a field, treat every reader of the OLD shape as a shape-consumer: audit each reader for an undefined-tolerant path (a missing field must become an explicit, REPORTED degradation, never a silent default) and keep a non-vacuity witness on every measurement that depends on the new field - the fixture's 'poseRate.pairs > 0' is the model, a measurement with zero samples reports FALSE, never true. (c) A seam is a RUNTIME contract, so a source-only change is not a change: the served artifact must be rebuilt and its identity (bytes + sha256) recorded, because a stale bundle silently serves the OLD shape - here the rebuild produced the five-field literal neatRacingDriftState={poseRad:...,slipAngleRad:...,speedMps:...,tickHz:...,tick:L.tick} in a 398,699-byte bundle (sha256 3C255A7F91A99AA8B3C7172B2BADCD23426DC63746A286E81778A16E33FFD9D8) for BOTH docs/assets/neatracing.bundle.js and examples/neatRacing/assets/neatracing.bundle.js. (d) For agent-maintenance-coordinator with browser-harness-specialist: add a lint that FAILS a browser fixture which reads a window.<debug> property that no production file ever writes (an unresolvable seam identifier), so the next dead branch is caught statically instead of by a rebase.

description: A mandated specialist co-sign on a multi-surface contract change converges in ROUNDS, and the productive pattern is to hand the reviewer the EXACT list of applied fixes with file:line anchors and ask for a CONFIRM-ONLY pass. The api-contract-reviewer co-sign for the Step 14N W3 five-field seam took 3 rounds (2 x REQUEST_CHANGES, then APPROVE), and round 2 existed only because round 1's fix list was itself INCOMPLETE - one live criterion was fixed while two sibling live rows were missed - because a reviewer can only confirm a change it can be shown. The dispatch contract reinforces the pattern: scripts/agent-customization/dispatch/build-dispatch-packet.mjs:18 sets PROMPT_LENGTH_MAX = 500 and resolvePromptLengthMax() returns 500 for moderate and complex slices (200 for trivial), so a dispatch prompt CANNOT inline a long fix list - the anchored brief must live in the RAG-indexed plan or artifact and the prompt must carry only the slice ID plus a compact anchor pointer.
evidence: THE CO-SIGN (recorded at plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md:9591-9592): 'the api-contract-reviewer co-sign (MANDATED by the W3 contract) took 3 rounds. Round 1 = REQUEST_CHANGES with 4 blocking findings: the live plan criterion (L2423) still mandated FOUR fields and the dated PATCH B-3 entry (L4003) said the seam must NOT grow a fifth; the fixture comment still said FIXED at four fields; BOTH shipped bundles still emitted the 4-field seam; the gate doc section 1 named the deleted car.driftYawOffset. Round 2 = REQUEST_CHANGES: the B-1 amendment was INCOMPLETE - the live RED-slice criterion (L2375) and the AC-087 row (L482) still said 4 fields, and the blocker-table B-3 row (L8984) asserted a now-false fact about L2423. Round 3 = APPROVE.' The same record then lists the applied fixes with their anchors: 'the live plan criteria (L2423, L2375), the AC-087 row (L482) and the blocker-table B-3 row (L8984) all state the FIVE-field seam; the dated PATCH B-3 entry's clause is WITHDRAWN by a dated SUPERSEDED bullet (L4004); the fixture comment and the gate doc section 1 were corrected; the bundle was rebuilt and the tracked copy refreshed.' THE DISPATCH BUDGET (read directly at capture time): scripts/agent-customization/dispatch/build-dispatch-packet.mjs:18 'export const PROMPT_LENGTH_MAX = 500;' with the docblock 'Prompts exceeding this limit are rejected to enforce RAG-based dispatch (short prompt + slice ID, not inline design context)'; :26 PROMPT_LENGTH_MAX_TRIVIAL = 200; :33 COMPLEXITY_LEVELS = ['trivial','moderate','complex']; :40 DEFAULT_COMPLEXITY = 'moderate'; :90-93 resolvePromptLengthMax() returns 200 for trivial and 500 otherwise; the MCP surface states the same contract at scripts/agent-customization/mcp/neataptic-dispatch-mcp.mjs:155-159 and :204-208 ('Trivial slices get a 200-character prompt limit; moderate/complex get 500'); the limit is enforced and REGRESSION-TESTED at scripts/agent-customization/dispatch/build-dispatch-packet.test.mjs:118-121 (resolvePromptLengthMax('moderate') === 500 and ('complex') === 500) and :215-267 (a 500-character prompt is accepted and a 501-character prompt is rejected with prompt_length_max 500, for both moderate and complex). THE LINK BETWEEN THE TWO FACTS IS MECHANICAL: with a 500-character cap the reviewer's brief cannot travel inside the dispatch prompt, so it must be anchored in the RAG-indexed plan - which is exactly where the reviewer read it, and exactly why the anchor list, not a prose narrative, is the artifact that makes a confirm-only pass possible.
followup_action: (a) PRODUCTIVE PATTERN, reusable for every mandated co-sign: before asking for a re-review, hand the reviewer the EXACT list of applied fixes as file:line anchors plus a one-line reason per anchor, and ask for a CONFIRM-ONLY pass ('confirm these N anchors, or return the specific anchor that is wrong'). This converts an open-ended re-read into a finite checklist and is what took the co-sign from a stalled round 2 to APPROVE in round 3. (b) The anchor list must come from a FULL enumeration of the affected rows BEFORE the first review - round 2 existed purely because the round-1 fix list was incomplete (L2375 and L482 were missed after L2423 was fixed), so the enumeration is the cheap preventive and the extra review rounds are the expensive symptom. (c) The 500-character dispatch budget is a FEATURE of RAG-based dispatch (short prompt + slice ID, not inline design context - build-dispatch-packet.mjs:13-18): put the brief in the RAG-indexed plan or artifact, keep the dispatch prompt to the slice ID plus a compact anchor pointer, and never try to inline a long fix list into the prompt - it will be rejected with prompt_length_max 500. (d) For agent-maintenance-coordinator: the builder has no field for a reviewer brief, so an anchored list currently has to be smuggled through the plan; consider an explicit review-brief field EXEMPT from the PROMPT_LENGTH_MAX check, so a co-sign can be dispatched with a machine-checked anchor list instead of a prose hand-off.

description: Tightening a GEOMETRIC BOUND silently invalidates the fixtures of every OTHER contract that was anchored to the old bound, not only the contracts that name the bound. The Step 14P slice P1-drift-rewire-road-surface moved the track-boundary containment bound from the outer grass-apron edge (halfWidth + NEATRACING_TRACK_GRASS_APRON_WIDTH_M) to the drivable-surface edge (the nearest segment driveable half width) to satisfy the AC-081 / AC-089 contract. Two contracts in the SAME test file that never mention the bound were anchored to it: the P0-3 / AC-079 drift-channel wipe contracts (a boundary bounce only fires OUTSIDE the bound, so the sliding fixture car must sit outside the NEW bound) and the closed Step P1-S7-C lat-5 interpretation pin (a car at lat 5 was byte-identical under the old bound and is now reseated onto the drivable edge). The reusable rule: when a bound, a threshold or a band edge moves, GREP THE WHOLE TEST SURFACE for every fixture anchored to that edge - not only the tests that name it - and record each re-anchored fixture as an explicit RE-BASELINE in the slice record; a fixture that is re-anchored silently is a contract that can rot without any failing assertion.
evidence: THE BOUND MOVE (recorded in the slice PlanUpdate at plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md, Step 14P / P1-drift-rewire-road-surface): resolveTrackBoundaryCar now reads the bound from nearestChord.halfWidthM (the outer edge of the road core plus the curb band) instead of halfWidth + NEATRACING_TRACK_GRASS_APRON_WIDTH_M, and the private reboundPastApronEdge was renamed reboundPastDrivableSurfaceEdge because the old name referenced the retired bound. THE SIBLING FIXTURE THAT HAD TO MOVE: the P0-3 drift-channel fixture (four it() blocks) seated its sliding car at outerApronBoundM + 1 (7.0 + 1); under the new bound that car is INSIDE the drivable surface, so NO bounce fires and the channel-wipe contracts would have failed - the fixture had to be re-anchored to drivableSurfaceEdgeM + 1. THE CLOSED-STEP PIN: the P1-S7-C red contract (recorded in plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.logs.md:2013 and confirmed by the plan at :818) had deliberately pinned the OUTER grass-apron bound with an untouched-at-lat-5 byte-identity assertion at ~88% confidence, and the closed step record at plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md:818-819 still describes that interpretation - the implementing slice must NOT rewrite the closed record, it must re-baseline the pin in its OWN record and let the later record supersede the earlier one. THE PROOF THAT THE COUPLING IS REAL (not theoretical): the bound was temporarily re-pointed at the retired outer-apron edge and the same targeted command reported 7 failed / 28 passed / 35 total - the failures were the three boundary contracts AND the four P0-3 drift-channel contracts, proving that a bound move reaches contracts that never name the bound. THE AUTHORISATION: the plan pre-authorised the case - the author decision D_Q8 states that if Step 14I has not landed the wave implements the SAME bound and Step 14I records the satisfaction, so the two steps never implement two different bounds - and the Step 14I P1-track-road-containment packet now carries that satisfaction_record.
followup_action: (a) When a bound, a threshold, a band edge or a magic offset moves, GREP the whole test surface for fixtures anchored to that edge before running anything: the failing-test count is NOT the discovery mechanism (a fixture re-anchored in the same edit hides the coupling), the grep is. (b) A fixture that must move because a BOUND moved is a RE-BASELINE, not a test fix: record it in the slice PlanUpdate with the old anchor, the new anchor and the reason, so the green slice can enter it in the shared re-baseline ledger instead of the change looking cosmetic. (c) When a later AC supersedes a pin recorded by a CLOSED step, do not rewrite the closed step record - the later slice record supersedes it explicitly and the closed step stays a true history. (d) The one-bound rule has a concrete guard: when two steps own the same bound, the second step records the SATISFACTION in the first step packet (satisfaction_record) and does NOT flip the first step status - the first step green slice owns the status and the served-page evidence. (e) For agent-maintenance-coordinator: a static helper that lists every test fixture constant derived from a bound (for example every FIXTURE_HALF_TRACK_WIDTH_M expression in a test file) would make the coupling greppable in one command.

description: RE-DERIVING a SHARED constant in an implementing slice invalidates the ratified literals of EVERY contract anchored to it, but the implementing slice owns only the SOURCE file - the re-baselined TEST literals usually belong to a LATER slice whose files_to_change cap may not even include the test files, so the re-baselining can end up OWNED BY NOBODY and the wave cannot close. The Step 14Q slice P1-drift-law-proportional re-derived the drift body yaw gain (0.5 -> 0.45) and the DECLARED pose envelope (0.3050 -> 0.30185 rad) in examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.ts. That single source change invalidated five ratified literals in THREE test files the slice does not own: the drift model suite (the anti-null gain pin expect(GAIN).toBe(0.5) and the proxy identity 0.04938855057460811), the service suite (the two envelope-derivation pins, the old committed-ceiling basis 0.225 and the pose 0.305) and the car pass suite (the DERIVED MAX_SLIP x GAIN pin 0.225). description: PUBLISHING a NEW DERIVED field on a SHARED state record turns that record into a MULTI-OWNER contract, but a slice packet with a tight files_to_change cap only names the OWNER of the field - it never names the OTHER modules that RECONSTRUCT the same record. The Step 14Q slice P1-drift-traction-scalar published the new named field tractionSeverity on the PhysicsCarState record in examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.ts (the ONLY file of the slice; the law computeTractionSeverity already existed in examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.ts through the sibling slice P1-drift-law-proportional). A construction sweep showed that examples/neatRacing/physics/collision.utils.ts REBUILDS a car state by SPREADING the previous record on the collision bounce (the drift channel is zeroed and the published slip is set to 0), so a bounced state carries the PRE-BOUNCE tractionSeverity for exactly ONE published frame, until the next stepPhysics tick recomputes it from the zeroed slip. collision.utils.ts is NOT in the slice files_to_change, so the residual could only be REPORTED, not patched - and the sibling field travelHeadingRad (published by Step 14P) already has the SAME characteristic, because the bounce recompose keeps the pre-bounce travel heading too. The reusable rule: an implementing slice that adds a field to a shared state record MUST SWEEP EVERY MODULE THAT CONSTRUCTS OR RECOMPOSES that record (not only the modules that READ it), and the slice packet should carry an explicit acceptance criterion for that sweep, because the READ-side consumers are usually listed in the AC while the CONSTRUCT-side ones are not. The zero per-frame allocation rule was NOT broken: a primitive number field on the already-allocated per-tick record adds no allocation.
evidence: THE CHANGE (examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.ts, the only production file of the slice): the PhysicsCarState interface gained the named field tractionSeverity (number); the spawn record publishes tractionSeverity 0; the tick pipeline computes computeTractionSeverity(nextSlipAngle, nextSpeedAfterTraction) as the new step 6 and publishes it on the returned state, where nextSlipAngle is the very number published as state.slipAngle and nextSpeedAfterTraction is the very number published as state.speed (the POST-traction speed, after the drift scrub and the off-road floor). THE CONSTRUCTION SWEEP: the grep for PhysicsCarState over examples/neatRacing returned the reconstruction sites in physics/collision.utils.ts (the displaceCar, recomposeCarWithVelocity and reboundPastDrivableSurfaceEdge helpers), in host/race-session.ts and in the test suites - EVERY one of them builds a record by SPREADING a previous record, so the new REQUIRED field breaks no type contract (npx tsc -p tsconfig.neatRacing.json --noEmit exits 0). description: BACKGROUND-AGENT COMPLETION NOTIFICATIONS CAN BE LOST ACROSS CLI SESSION BOUNDARIES, and an orchestrator that treats no-notification as no-progress will sit idle for hours. During Step 14Q the slice P1-drift-traction-scalar (04-implementing, background agent 34f5a687) genuinely finished at about 2026-10-27T19:45Z: it wrote its structured-v1 report, went idle, appended its PlanUpdate to the plan and its learning event to the log. But the completion wake-up never reached the orchestrator turn loop across a CLI session boundary, so the orchestrator stayed idle for about 9 hours while the user observed that nothing was running, and a concurrently failed RAG re-index (SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked, exit 1) went unretried because the idle orchestrator never checked its background shells either. The queue stalled for the full window even though the work was DONE. The reusable rule: for a session orchestrator, the absence of a completion notification is an UNKNOWN STATE, never evidence of no progress - notifications are a convenience, not a contract.
evidence: THE INCIDENT: user message at about 2026-10-28T04:56Z reported NOTHING is running after hours of downtime; a list_agents cross-check showed agent 34f5a687 idle with 33548s elapsed and its full SUCCESS report unread (total_turns 1, the report was there the whole time), plus a separate correctly-scoped agent 82bbbbae (slice P1-drift-law-repin, agent 14N-K-impl-14Q-repin) already running under its own dispatch. Shell history showed the parallel RAG re-index (shellId 1395) had failed with SQLITE_BUSY exit 1 hours earlier and had never been retried. THE RECOVERY (under one hour): the unread structured-v1 report was read and reconciled, both slice statuses were flipped to DONE in the plan with embedded evidence, a NEW-TOP validation-evidence entry was appended, the SQLITE_BUSY re-index was retried successfully (scanned 2010, indexed 2, chunks 683; embed embedded 688, skipped 27476), and the queue resumed at the next boundary (P1-drift-law-code-green dispatch) with no work lost and no duplicate dispatched against a live agent. THE ROOT CAUSE: background-agent completion notifications are delivered by the runtime between turns; a session boundary / compaction between the notification and the next orchestrator turn dropped the wake-up, and no fallback existed. THE MITIGATION NOW STANDING (recorded in the plan validation evidence as a standing mitigation): an orchestrator MUST cross-check list_agents against its expected dispatch queue on EVERY turn and after every session boundary or compaction, MUST immediately read the structured-v1 of any new idle agent, MUST check its own background shell completions, and MUST re-run index:build / index:embed when a plan edit landed without a confirmed successful index rebuild.
followup_action: (a) For 00-helping / agent-maintenance-coordinator: a durable background-queue ledger in the session store (one row per dispatched agent with its expected slice, dispatch time and last observed status) would turn notification loss into a bounded reconciliation instead of an hours-long stall; the orchestrator reconciliation loop then reads only the ledger rows whose agent is not confirmed running. (b) For orchestrators at every tier: after waking from a session boundary, ALWAYS assume notifications may have been lost and start with one list_agents cross-check plus a background-shell completion check before dispatching anything new. (c) For planning: a slice that dispatches one background implementation agent per slice (the slim dispatch mandate) amplifies the cost of a single lost notification, because the whole slice queue is serialized behind the orchestrator turn loop - queue recovery should be a standard first-turn action, not an incident response.

description: THE RED CONTRACT SCHEMA DOES NOT REQUIRE A DISCRIMINATING, CURRENTLY-FAILING OBSERVABLE, SO A STEP PACKET CAN BE AUTHORED WITH VACUOUS (GREEN-ON-ARRIVAL) CONTRACTS. The two NEW [PLANNED] packets in plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md - Step 14S (the MOMENTUM law, slice P1-momentum-red) and Step 14T (the TURN-RATE laws, slice P1-turnrate-red) - author 8 RED contracts (RED-1..RED-4 per step), but a fresh independent verification found that 5 of the 8 are ALREADY SATISFIED by the current build and are therefore GREEN-ON-ARRIVAL: 14S RED-2, 14S RED-3, 14S RED-4, 14T RED-2 and 14T RED-4. Only 14S RED-1 (the momentum law does not exist), 14T RED-1 (the turn rate grows with the speed) and 14T RED-3 (the turn-rate-percent channel does not exist) fail against the current source. ROOT CAUSE: the 7 ratified Step 14Q RED contracts ALL open with an explicit NON-VACUITY GUARD (both lanes must really slide), so a relational assertion can never be satisfied by a flat or zero lane; NEITHER 14S nor 14T requires such a guard, so a RELATIONAL contract (STRICTLY DEEPER at a higher speed / STRICTLY LOWER at a higher speed) carrying only a BOUNDS or a PRESERVATION guard was authored that today's build already satisfies.
evidence: (1) THE FIVE VACUOUS CONTRACTS: the independent verification of the 8 RED contracts in the two [PLANNED] packets (Step 14S slice P1-momentum-red at plan lines 3574-3580; Step 14T slice P1-turnrate-red at plan lines 3732-3738) found ALREADY GREEN against the current source: 14S RED-2 (the committed slide is STRICTLY DEEPER at a high speed than at a low speed and EXACTLY 0 at a standstill - already true because the slide ramps at the SPEED-PROPORTIONAL entry rate), 14S RED-3 (the slide stays inside the depth budget and the severity inside the closed unit interval - a pure BOUNDS guard the current model already satisfies), 14S RED-4 (the live tick applies the momentum - a RELATIONAL comparison that already holds), 14T RED-2 (the steer axis value the drift model reads is UNCHANGED and the softened user turn rate still produces a committed slide - the PRESERVATION half is already true) and 14T RED-4 (the AI adoption is BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING - a pure PRESERVATION contract). Only 14S RED-1, 14T RED-1 and 14T RED-3 fail. (2) THE RATIFIED PRECEDENT THAT PREVENTS VACUITY - all 7 Step 14Q RED contracts open with an explicit NON-VACUITY GUARD in examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.test.ts, asserted FIRST: both lanes must really slide at :1567-1569 (contract [RED-14Q-1-LAW-SPEED-AXIS] at :1543); the low-speed lane must really slide, a zero slide would satisfy the ceiling vacuously, at :1592-1594 ([RED-14Q-2-SPEED-PROPORTIONAL-DEPTH] at :1576); both lanes must REACH the target slip, otherwise the comparison would be vacuous, at :1621-1623 ([RED-14Q-3A-ENTRY-RAMP-SPEED] at :1606); and the same guard shape at :1653, :1690, :1726, :1748, :986 and :1114. NEITHER 14S nor 14T contains an equivalent guard, and 14S RED-2 and 14T RED-1 are exactly the STRICTLY-RELATIONAL shape that the 14Q guard exists to protect. (3) THE CONTRIBUTING GATE GAP - a [PLANNED] packet is INVISIBLE to the structural sub-gates: scripts/agent-customization/gates/step-packet.gate.mjs:100-101 skips every YAML block whose status is not WIP (if (statusValue !== 'WIP') continue;), and scripts/agent-customization/gates/plan-slice-quality.gate.mjs:74-78 does the same, so the consolidated slice-advancement gate reports a TRIVIAL 4/4 structural pass for a [PLANNED] packet that has never been executed. (4) NO MACHINE GATE TESTS THAT A RED CONTRACT ACTUALLY FAILS: scripts/agent-customization/gates/red-test-confirmation.gate.mjs is a Tier-2 standalone-descriptor that returns pass TRUE unconditionally (mode: standalone-descriptor, minimumRedTests: 2) and never executes the contracts against the current source, so a vacuous RED contract cannot be caught by any gate in the inventory - only by an independent verification like this one.

description: The `plan` corpus family of the Cortex index is `plans/**/*.md` (ignoring `plans/completed/**`), NOT `plans/*.plans.md`, so the plan-family stale set can contain NON-`.plans.md` members: a targeted reindex that passes only `plans/<name>.plans.md` leaves `plans/README.md` and `plans/Roadmap.md` stale and the `cortex-index` gate STILL FAILS. Separately, `embed-index.mjs` configures NO busyTimeout on its libSQL client, so transient replica-lock contention surfaces as an immediate `SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked` exit 1 that must be retried externally and never resolved by killing the holder.

description: THE NGE GROWTH PATH RANDOMIZES HIDDEN-NODE ACTIVATIONS FROM BARE Math.random() - A SRC-LEVEL DETERMINISM GAP WITH NO RNG HOOK, COMPENSATED AT THE ENGINE LAYER. NGE growth adds hidden nodes via network.mutate.handlers.utils.ts createHiddenNode (~:145-149), which calls node-level mutate(MOD_ACTIVATION) -> applyActivationMutation (src/architecture/node/node.ts:164) drawing the squash from bare Math.random() (verified: MUTATION_HANDLER_TABLE and the function body expose no rng hook, and the default method set has multiple entries so the draw is live), so every growth-added hidden node carried a RANDOM activation and post-growth scoring drifted across twin engines AND repeat runs even with a fully-seeded pipeline. Root-cause methodology that found it (reusable): probe-driven bisection with geneId-stripped JSON equality (Network twins differ only in cosmetic geneId fields from a shared global counter), repeated-run comparison, then node-level field comparison which showed biases/weights bit-identical while squashes randomized per run/instance (sinusoid/absolute/relu vs bipolar/sinusoid/softsign etc.). P2-S3-A engine-layer compensation (the activation-policy-immutability contract): capture pre-growth squashes beside the rollback bookkeeping, restore them post-cycle for surviving nodes, pin the Node default (Activation.logistic) for growth-added nodes BEFORE any post-mutation scoring - twin decision replay becomes bit-reproducible at zero RNG-stream cost. CAVEAT for later slices: Node.toJSON serializes squash.name while Node.fromJSON resolves squash by KEY (node.ts ~:1513 / ~:1544-1554), so a JSON round-trip restores activations as identity (pre-existing, silent).
evidence: the twin-decision-replay tests RED pre-fix -> GREEN post-fix (examples/neatRacing/ai/runtime.adaptation.test.ts ~:253 and ~:286; lane 69/69 final); probe methodology constraints recorded in the P2-S3-A PlanUpdate: jest probes must live inside testMatch trees (src/benchmarks/examples/testing - never tmp/), console output requires JEST_ALLOW_ALL_LOGS=1 via cmd /c (testing/jest-setup.ts suppression), probes deleted after use; the full finding chain is recorded in the P2-S3-A PlanUpdate in plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md (2026-11-06).

description: THE EDIT TOOL'S PARAMETER LAYER IS A PARTIAL ESCAPE DECODER: IT DECODES THE \r AND \n ESCAPES IN old_str/new_str BUT DOES NOT UNESCAPE BACKSLASHES, AND ITS WRITE PATH NORMALIZES LINE ENDINGS TO CRLF. THREE CONSEQUENCES, ALL MEASURED IN THE STEP-23B B-4 PATCH CYCLE: (1) A BACKSLASH IS LITERAL - THE RAW-BACKSLASH COUNT IN old_str IS THE LITERAL-BACKSLASH COUNT THAT IS MATCHED: a 2-raw-backslash old_str matches a run of 2 literal backslashes, while 3, 4 and 8 raw backslashes match NOTHING; (2) AN OVERSIZED old_str DEGENERATES TO A SAFE NO-OP - it neither writes nor errors, the bytes simply never change (the failure is SILENT and a success message is returned); (3) THE REPAIR PATTERN IS THE CHUNKED-SENTINEL EDIT - cut the target region at unique sentinel boundaries and land ONE SMALL, BACKSLASH-LIGHT CHUNK PER EDIT instead of one giant old_str. description: A TIER-3 REVIEWER REQUIRED A FIX THAT THE SLICE'S OWN ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA HAD DEFERRED, AND THE RESOLUTION WAS AN EXPLICIT OCCURRENCE-SPLIT PLAN-DEVIATION RECORD (NOT a silent obey and NOT a silent refusal): the plan's AC said the agentCount-resolution drift 'is RECORDED as a Step-24 concern and is NOT fixed in this slice', while the round-1 Tier-3 reviewer returned FIX 1 (HIGH, blocking) requiring the MODE-BOOT half of that drift to be fixed IN THIS slice - the AI branch of the mode switch booted the adaptation session at the GOAL machine's level while the fresh round booted at the carried ROUND level, so the session fleet and the seam team layout disagreed with the round fleet (at rung 2 the background carrier network drove a REAL agent car - the carrier-beyond-fleet invariant broken; at rung 3 the agent cars owned NO network). THE ADOPTED RESOLUTION (recorded, NOT silent): the deferral named TWO occurrences of ONE defect. Occurrence (i) the MODE BOOT - the session is created FRESH there (no evolution is discarded, no promotion-round semantics involved) and the slice's OWN session-creation rule already prescribed the round's own boot level, so the AI branch was the ONE place violating the slice's own rule; fixing it COMPLETES the rule instead of expanding the scope. Occurrence (ii) the PROMOTION REBASE at browser-entry.ts:2332 (restartSimWorkerRound(decision.rebaseRung)) - the round reboots on the promoted rung while the session keeps its old level, and re-levelling there would DISCARD the carrier's evolved network (the session exposes NO grow/adopt API), so it stays Step 24's (P4-S2-promotion-round). The fix is a bit-identical NO-OP on the ordinary AI path (the AI lane starts at rung 1, where the goal level and the round level coincide). THE LESSON: when a reviewer requires a fix that an AC deferred, do NOT silently obey and do NOT silently refuse - SPLIT the deferred defect into its occurrences, fix the occurrence the slice's own rule already covers, keep the occurrence whose fix would discard evolved state, and RECORD the split as an explicit PLAN-DEVIATION RECORD naming the reviewer AND the plan/AC as the two authorities; a deferral that names a defect but NOT its OCCURRENCES is under-specified and WILL be re-litigated by the next reviewer.

description: RE-INDENTING A PlanUpdate YAML SECTION WITH THE edit TOOL BY ANCHORING ON THE INDENT IS UNSAFE: an indent-only anchor is a PARTIAL-LINE PREFIX anchor, so it can match the WRONG occurrence, it can silently NO-OP while the tool reports success, and it cannot express or match the artifacts it leaves behind (a bare CR 0x0D is untypeable in a literal old_str, and a shell-side rewrite is out of contract for an agent role). THE WORKING RECIPE: a FULL MULTI-LINE UNIQUE-CONTEXT anchor (never an indent-only anchor), ONE edit call for the whole block, a BYTE SCAN after every edit (0 lone LF, no BOM, CRLF preserved), and a FENCE-PAIRING check; verify the anchor's uniqueness with a READ-ONLY occurrence count BEFORE the edit; and do NOT shell-normalize bytes (edit/create only for agent roles).

description: process.resourceUsage().maxRSS IS A PROCESS-LIFETIME HIGH-WATER MARK OVER GC-TIMING-SENSITIVE ALLOCATION, SO IT IS NOT MONOTONE IN WORKLOAD SIZE - AND A SINGLE-SAMPLE FROZEN BASELINE IS THEREFORE AN UNSOUND COMPARISON BASIS FOR IT. MEASURED ON THE P1-S1-4 GREEN LANE: the corpus SHRANK (2,080 -> 1,848 documents, 33,025 -> 20,899 chunks, temporary replica 111,788,032 -> 70,127,616 bytes) and the build got 2.8x FASTER (elapsedMs 87,347 -> 34,659), yet EVERY post-change run exceeded EVERY pre-change run. THE SAME CORPUS, MEASURED TWICE 51 ms APART IN ELAPSED TIME, DIFFERED BY 37,363,712 B (6.45 %) - so the metric's own noise is an order of magnitude larger than the effect being judged. THE POST-CHANGE DISTRIBUTION IS BIMODAL (4 runs at 592.5-595.5 MB, 3 runs at 629.9-630.7 MB, a ~34.4 MB MODE STEP) and its own spread is 5.3x THE DELTA BEING JUDGED. THE PEAK IS DOMINATED BY CORPUS-INDEPENDENT TERMS - the ts-morph Project over the unchanged 516-file ts-source family (never dispose()d) and the whole-build ts-chunk Map - so removing the 20.9 MB session snapshot DELETED a large-object-space allocation that used to force early major GCs and stretch the run to ~85 s; the shorter, lower-allocation run then lets the V8 old generation reach a HIGHER high-water mark. THIS IS THE CLASSIC 'A SMALLER CORPUS CAN HAVE A HIGHER PEAK RSS' CASE FOR A V8 WORKLOAD, AND IT IS WHY THE AC-203-GREEN PEAK-RSS CLAUSE, AS WRITTEN, IS NOT SATISFIABLE: it compares one n=1 frozen sample (585,711,616 B) against a 6.45 %-spread distribution, so the criterion is not satisfiable as written rather than the change being wrong. description: AN INCREMENTAL INDEX UPDATER THAT KEYS FRESHNESS ON CONTENT (mtime / sha) RATHER THAN ON FAMILY ASSIGNMENT LEAVES A FAMILY RENAME STALE ON CONTENT-UNCHANGED FILES. MEASURED: the live index still carried the RETIRED `benchmark` family with 22 documents (the benchmarks/**/*.test.ts files, indexed 2026-10-11) while the new `test` family held only 317 of the contract's 339 documents, even though ALL 339 rows matched disk EXACTLY in mtime_ms and file_size. THE MECHANISM: the updater's corpus identity is computed from the documents table as `file_path|sha256|mtime_ms|file_size` (rag-index/update-rag.mjs:219-228) - the doc_family column is NOT part of the key - so a family REASSIGNMENT that changes no file byte is INVISIBLE to the freshness check, the computed hash still equals the stored hash, and the build-graph stage is SKIPPED, leaving the stale family assignment in the index. THE CONTENT KEY IS CORRECT FOR WHAT IT MEASURES (has the file changed?) AND WRONG FOR WHAT THE CONTRACT NEEDS (which family does this file belong to NOW?) - and the two questions coincide exactly when a family is renamed or a file is re-assigned WITHOUT touching its bytes, which is precisely the shape of the corpus-contract migration this plan performs. THE CONSEQUENCE IS A SILENT PARITY HOLE: the retired family keeps owning documents in the LIVE index while the contract says it owns zero, and NO freshness signal fires, because every row is content-current.

description: THE CORPUS IDENTITY THE PLAN RELIES ON AS ITS LIKE-FOR-LIKE PROOF HASHES ONLY family:documentCount - THE CHUNK COUNT IS NOT IN THE KEY - AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT DEFINES THAT IDENTITY IS OUTSIDE THE BOUNDARY OF THE SLICE THAT OBSERVED THE BLIND SPOT. THE IDENTITY IN THE REPOSITORY PROBE IS sha256 OVER THE LINES family:documentCount AND NOTHING ELSE (rag-index/__tests__/fixtures/build-memory-probe.mjs:160-167): no chunk count, no per-family chunk census, no file content, no mtime, no chunking input. CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED: the chunk count MOVED 20,899 -> 20,977 between the two GREEN lanes while the identity did NOT move, because the family census was unchanged (9 families / 1,848 documents in both arms) - so two captures that chunk the SAME corpus DIFFERENTLY SHARE an identity, and the identity CANNOT be used as a like-for-like chunking proof. THE PLAN ALREADY SUSPECTED HALF OF IT (corpus.identity is a CENSUS-OF-COUNTS hash rather than a content hash - so P1-S1-4 must compare the FOUR MEASURED NUMBERS and not identity equality) and the second GREEN lane recorded it as V-OBS-022. THE BOUNDARY DEFECT IS THE PART THAT BLOCKS THE FIX: P1-S1-4's files_to_change are rag-index/__tests__/corpus-contract.red.test.mjs, rag-index/__tests__/fixtures/build-memory-baseline.json and rag-index/build-entity-graph.test.mjs - the probe fixture that DEFINES the identity is NOT among them, so the GREEN lane that discovered the defect CANNOT extend the key; and the RED home only asserts the SHAPE of the identity (a 64-hex string) and never binds it to the chunk count, so no test in the suite would catch the blind spot either. description: THE FROZEN TEST HOST'S jest.unstable_mockModule MOCK OF './ts-chunker-v2.mjs' EXPOSES ONLY chunkTypeScriptSourcesV2, SO A NAMED IMPORT OF ANY ADDITIONAL EXPORT (chunkTypeScriptSourcesV2Stream) IS A MODULE LINK ERROR UNDER THAT MOCK; THE PRODUCTION CODE MUST THEREFORE USE A NAMESPACE IMPORT PLUS A FEATURE-DETECTED FLAT FALLBACK. THE COST IS TWO SHAPES IN PRODUCTION AND ZERO UNIT COVERAGE OF THE STREAMING PATH: EVERY TEST SILENTLY EXERCISES THE FALLBACK, so the production streaming path - the one that satisfies the per-document residency contract - IS NEVER TESTED, AND THE FALLBACK RE-MATERIALISES THE WHOLE CHUNK ARRAY, i.e. exactly the O(corpus) residency the slice was chartered to remove. THE LESSON: A FROZEN MOCK SURFACE IS A HARD CONSTRAINT ON THE PRODUCTION IMPORT SHAPE AND MUST BE CLEARED (extend the mock surface, then retire the fallback) rather than worked around with a permanent untested dual path.
evidence: SOURCE FACTS (read-only, re-verified by this capture): rag-index/build-index.test.mjs:57-59 - jest.unstable_mockModule('./ts-chunker-v2.mjs', () => ({ chunkTypeScriptSourcesV2: mockChunkTypeScriptSourcesV2 })) - the mock factory exposes EXACTLY ONE export. The production file responds with a NAMESPACE import, rag-index/build-index.mjs:48 import * as tsChunkerV2 from './ts-chunker-v2.mjs';, and the streaming path is FEATURE-DETECTED at :468 (typeof tsChunkerV2.chunkTypeScriptSourcesV2Stream === 'function') with the stream consumed at :500 - so the FLAT FALLBACK is what runs whenever the feature probe is false, which is ALWAYS under the frozen mock. The new streaming export exists in production: rag-index/ts-chunker-v2.mjs:124 export async function* chunkTypeScriptSourcesV2Stream(options), with the flat API at :91 iterating that same generator, so both shapes share one implementation. THE PLAN'S OWN RECORD: plan :1810 (item 11) records the flat fallback as the ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the no-deferred-cleanup rule - used ONLY when chunkTypeScriptSourcesV2Stream is absent from the imported module, which happens under the FROZEN test host whose jest.unstable_mockModule mock exposes ONLY chunkTypeScriptSourcesV2; 'A named import of the streaming export would be a MODULE LINK ERROR under that mock and would break the frozen suite' - and flags it as finding F3. The findings table in plan item 10 records F2 (MED) - 'the PRODUCTION streaming path has ZERO unit coverage - rag-index/build-index.test.mjs mocks ONLY chunkTypeScriptSourcesV2, so every test exercises the FLAT fallback' - and F3 (MED) - 'the FLAT fallback re-materialises the whole flat chunk array - the shape AC-203-G-IMPL-B forbids - so the code carries TWO shapes' - both FORWARDED to P1-S3-3 in plan item 13 (the GREEN lane must add the streaming-path coverage and align the comparators). description: RELEASING THE ts-morph AST ALONE DOES NOT LOWER PEAK RSS: THE PRE-GC CONTROL ARM MEASURED A MEDIAN OF 594,739,200 B - WORSE THAN THE 585,920,512 B BEFORE-CAPTURE - WHILE THE FORCED FULL GC AT THE RELEASE BOUNDARY IS THE MECHANISM THAT ACTUALLY RETURNS THE PAGES (10-RUN POOLED MEDIAN 568,799,232 B, 16,912,384 B BELOW THE FROZEN CEILING 585,711,616 B, 10/10 RUNS BELOW). THE LESSON FOR EVERY BOUNDED-MEMORY REMEDIATION: THE RESOURCE-RELEASE CALL AND THE PAGE-RETURN MECHANISM ARE TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, AND A REMEDIATION JUDGED ON THE RESOURCE STATE ALONE MEASURES NO (OR A WORSE) PEAK-RSS IMPROVEMENT - THE RELEASE MECHANISM MUST BE SPECIFIED AND MEASURED ALONGSIDE THE RESOURCE RELEASE.
evidence: THE MEASUREMENTS (P1-S3-4 lane; the verdict against the ceiling remains the P1-S3-3 GREEN lane's obligation and this event does NOT claim it): the PRE-GC CONTROL ARM measured a MEDIAN of 594,739,200 B, i.e. WORSE than the 585,920,512 B before-capture; with the FORCED FULL GC at the release boundary the 10-run POOLED MEDIAN is 568,799,232 B, which is 16,912,384 B (2.89 %) BELOW the unchanged frozen ceiling 585,711,616 B with 10/10 runs below (plans/cortex-plan-first-retrieval.plans.md item 6 table: 5 primary runs median 569,085,952 B plus 5 corroborating runs median 568,512,512 B, pooled over 10 runs; the same pooled median is restated in the lane handoff refresh at plan :2367). Back-to-back single captures on the SAME corpus read 585,920,512 B BEFORE -> 569,221,120 B AFTER (-16,699,392 B, -2.85 %) and 570,617,856 B on an independent re-run; the build time is unchanged (32.6-33.4 s after vs 30.2 s before); every one of the ten runs reproduced the same replica (71,806,976 B) and the same chunk count (21,013). THE MECHANISM IN THE PRODUCTION BYTES (read-only, re-verified by this capture): rag-index/build-index.mjs:534 calls forceHeapRelease() at the ts-source family boundary and :551-553 defines it with v8.setFlagsFromString('--expose-gc') - the forced full GC at the release boundary IS the mechanism that returns the pages, and the plan records it as BEST-EFFORT (plan :1737 and :2367). THE AST RELEASE ITSELF IS REAL AND SEPARATE (plan item 1): the new exported releaseTypeScriptProject(project) in rag-index/ts-chunker.mjs releases through the ONLY surfaces ts-morph 27.0.2 exposes (project.removeSourceFile(sourceFile) per source file, then project.getLanguageService().compilerObject.dispose()), because the Project has NO dispose() and NO forget(); the empirical confirmation that the compiler is no longer resident at chunk time is the pre-chunking resident set 104,728 KB BEFORE -> 61,212 KB AFTER (60,888 KB on an independent re-run). MEASUREMENT PROVENANCE, STATED HONESTLY: the pre-GC control-arm median (594,739,200 B) is quoted from the P1-S3-4 lane's control arm (its measurement artifacts live under the gitignored tmp/ path - plan item 12); THIS CAPTURE RE-VERIFIED THE PRODUCTION BYTES AND THE PLAN'S RECORDED POST-GC MATRIX FIRST-HAND AND RE-RAN NO MEASUREMENT. SIBLING IN THIS LOG (the prior, SUPERSEDED mechanism statement): learn-20261115-p1s1-4-iter2-ts-morph-project-never-disposed-27mb-drop-realised-as-9mb - which recorded that the expected ~27 MB drop realised as only -9,195,520 B; THIS EVENT RECORDS THE RESOLUTION OF THAT MECHANISM QUESTION - the drop is realised ONLY when the forced GC at the release boundary is in place.
followup_action: Owner 05-green-testing (slice P1-S3-3): re-measure the SAME N>=5 median arm against the UNCHANGED ceiling 585,711,616 B - do NOT accept the P1-S3-4 sample and do NOT single-run it (the per-run spread is 15-18 MB and a single run proves nothing); EXTEND - never regenerate - the frozen fixture rag-index/__tests__/fixtures/build-memory-baseline.json with the A5-permitted additive multi-sample statistics. Owner 04-implementing: when a bounded-memory remediation is designed, the release MECHANISM MUST BE SPECIFIED ALONGSIDE THE RESOURCE RELEASE - name the forced full GC at the release boundary as part of the contract and MEASURE THE PRE-GC CONTROL ARM SEPARATELY, because a remediation measured without the GC looks like a REGRESSION (594,739,200 B, worse than the 585,920,512 B before-capture) and would be rejected as ineffective. description: AN IDEMPOTENT SKIP MASKED A STAGE THAT FAILS DETERMINISTICALLY. THE `npm run rag:update` CHAIN SKIPS `build-graph` WHENEVER `computeCorpusHash()` MATCHES `corpus-hash.json`, AND THAT HASH CARRIES NO `doc_family` - SO THE STAGE WAS NEVER EXERCISED AGAINST THE PUBLISHED 9-FAMILY CORPUS CONTRACT, AND THE PRIOR LANE'S OWN RECORDED `build-graph: skipped (0ms)` READ LIKE A PASS. THE STAGE REMAINED BROKEN UNTIL AN UNRELATED EDIT TO THE PLAN FILE CHANGED THE HASH AND FORCED IT TO RUN, AT WHICH POINT IT ABORTED THE WHOLE CHAIN WITH A DETERMINISTIC EXIT-134 V8 HEAP OOM (TWO RUNS, IDENTICAL). THE LESSON: A STAGE THAT IS SKIPPED BY AN IDEMPOTENCY HASH IS NOT TESTED, AND A SKIP IS NOT A PASS - A SKIP MASKS THE STAGE'S BEHAVIOUR ON THE CURRENT CORPUS UNTIL SOMETHING UNRELATED INVALIDATES THE HASH. A SKIP MUST BE READ AS 'THIS STAGE DID NOT RUN', AND A CONTRACT THAT PUBLISHES A NEW CORPUS SHAPE MUST EITHER INVALIDATE THE HASH THAT GUARDS THE STAGES THAT CONSUME IT OR BE VERIFIED AGAINST THOSE STAGES IN THE SAME LANE THAT PUBLISHES IT.
evidence: THE MECHANISM (read-only, verified by this capture): `rag-index/update-rag.mjs` computes the corpus hash over `file_path|sha256|mtime_ms|file_size` - THERE IS NO `doc_family` IN THE HASH - and skips `build-graph` on a match; the `P1-S3-4` lane's own recorded `rag:update` shows `build-graph: skipped (0ms)`, so the stage was NEVER RUN against the published 9-family contract. THE FAILURE (this lane, TWO RUNS, IDENTICAL): `build: ok (1234ms)`, `prewarm-embed: ok (5596ms)`, `build-terms: ok (99384ms)`, `build-graph: failed (24351ms)`, EXIT STATUS 134, `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory` at 8191.7 MB, with `snapshot` and `validate` CANCELLED. THE ROOT CAUSE IS MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHESISED: `rag-index/build-entity-graph.mjs:373-396` (`buildHeadingTextMap`) re-reads the ENTIRE source file for EVERY doc entity and retains `content.slice(char_start, char_end)` in `headingsByDoc`; EACH RETAINED V8 SlicedString PINS ITS ENTIRE PARENT, so a 9.3 MB parent is pinned once per entity. THE ACCOUNTING: 6,584 file reads totalling 5,239,687,219 BYTES READ FROM DISK out of only 25,845,342 bytes of actual file content - A 203x READ AMPLIFICATION - dominated by `plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.logs.md` (9,311,682 bytes x 525 entities, about 4.89 GB of redundant reads); measured PEAK WORKING SET 11,324,051,456 BYTES (10.80 GiB). IT IS HEAP-CAP-BOUND, NOT LOGIC-BOUND: the SAME stage exits 0 at `--max-old-space-size=12288` (25,644 ms; 10,277 entities / 25,957 edges), and the SAME cap explains the recorded baseline's TWO OOM-crashing Jest suites (`graph-term.turso.test.mjs` and `build-entity-graph.red.test.mjs`, 0 tests each), which BOTH PASS at 12,288 MB (2 suites / 9 tests). THE DEFECT IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO HEAD (the only diff in that file is the `P1-S1-3` `DOC_ENTITY_SOURCES` -> `CORPUS_SOURCES` swap) AND `P1-S1-3` IS EXONERATED BY AN A/B MEASUREMENT: the PUBLISHED 9-family contract yields 6,584 doc entities against the HEAD 7-family list's 11,734 - STRICTLY LESS PRESSURE. THE FILE IS IN NO SLICE'S `files_to_change`, SO THE DEFECT IS UNOWNED AND UNBOUNDED. TWO SIBLING FACTS CAPTURED IN THE SAME LANE: (i) the `AC-203-D-GREEN` criterion names a RED home `rag-index/__tests__/rag-update-memory.red.test.mjs` that DOES NOT EXIST, because `P1-S3-1` and `P1-S3-2` are still `[PLANNED]` and A6's `dispatch_order` omits both - a GREEN lane must not author a RED-by-name home; (ii) the convergence tracker's `extractLatestValidationEvidence` truncates the `## Latest validation evidence` body at the NEXT HEADING OF ANY LEVEL, so the `P1-S3-4` canonical marker at plan line 1849 lies OUTSIDE the scanned region (1253-1726) and the tracker reports a VACUOUS `iterationCount: 0` for that slice. MEASUREMENT PROVENANCE, STATED HONESTLY: the byte-identity instruments and the N>=5 memory arms are the P1-S3-3 lane's own artifacts under the gitignored `tmp/` path; this capture re-verified the production bytes and the plan's recorded matrix first-hand and RE-RAN NO MEASUREMENT.
followup_action: Owner 01-planning (BINDING, THIS LANE'S FORWARD POINTER - NOT a re-dispatch of 04-implementing): the plan amendment must open a NEW OWNING SLICE for `rag-index/build-entity-graph.mjs` with a BOUNDED-MEMORY CRITERION for the entity stage - the file is in NO slice's `files_to_change`, so the defect that aborts the chain has no owner and no bound (the `V-OBS-013` / `V-OBS-025` lineage is unowned). The amendment must ALSO route `P1-S3-1` and `P1-S3-2` before `P1-S3-3` (or redefine the 'GREEN BY NAME' predicate), own the forwarded F1-F7 streaming obligations, and repair the `P1-S3-4` canonical marker placement. Owner 04-implementing: WHEN A STAGE IS GUARDED BY AN IDEMPOTENCY HASH, THE HASH MUST INCLUDE EVERY INPUT DIMENSION THAT CHANGES THE STAGE'S BEHAVIOUR (here: `doc_family`), OR THE STAGE MUST BE RUN AT LEAST ONCE AGAINST EACH PUBLISHED CORPUS SHAPE IN THE SAME LANE THAT PUBLISHES IT - A SKIP IS NOT A PASS, AND A GREEN EVIDENCE TABLE MUST RECORD A SKIPPED STAGE AS 'DID NOT RUN', NEVER AS A PASS. Owner 01-planning / 05-green-testing (BINDING): a GREEN criterion that names a RED home BY FILENAME MUST BE CHECKED FOR EXISTENCE AT PLAN-AMENDMENT TIME. Owner 00-helping / agent-maintenance-coordinator: the convergence tracker should scan the `## Latest validation evidence` SECTION to its end rather than truncating at the next heading of any level, and should VALIDATE CANONICAL MARKER PLACEMENT at gate time - the current behaviour silently reports `iterationCount: 0` for a slice whose marker sits outside the region, which makes a live tracker defect look like a vacuous pass. Owner 05-green-testing (THIS LANE, DONE): the memory arm IS met and the chain failure is NOT, so `P1-S3-3` stays `[PLANNED]`, NOT `[DONE]`.
resolution: OPEN (2026-11-16). The MECHANISM is established and quantified by measurement, but the DEFECT is UNOWNED and UNFIXED: the `build-graph` stage still aborts the whole chain deterministically (exit 134) at the ambient 8,192 MB cap and no slice owns `rag-index/build-entity-graph.mjs`. NOT DISCHARGED BY THIS EVENT: `AC-203-D-GREEN` (unsatisfiable as written - its RED home does not exist) and `AC-206-B` (unmeasurable - its per-stage peak clause depends on the never-implemented `AC-203-C` / `P1-S3-2`). DISCHARGED: THE MEMORY BOUND ITSELF - the post-remediation N>=5 PRIMARY median is 563,331,072 BYTES against the UNCHANGED ceiling 585,711,616 BYTES (22,380,544 BYTES / 3.821 % HEADROOM, 10/10 RUNS BELOW, NO ALLOWANCE OF ANY KIND), and the frozen fixture was EXTENDED (never regenerated) with `multiSample.postRemediation`.

description: AC-203-C asks for a per-stage peak figure measured from the stage PROCESS itself, and the two facts that shape the whole implementation were MEASURED, not assumed. First, a parent process CANNOT observe a child peak RSS: the runner own process.resourceUsage().maxRSS read 43416 KB while the reaped child peak was 8894570496 bytes, so a parent-side estimate is impossible and the figure has to be produced INSIDE the stage process. Second, the natural in-child mechanism - a process.on(exit) hook that reports the child own maxRSS - fires ONLY on a normal exit or an uncaught throw: process.exit(3) published 45408256 bytes and an uncaught throw published 45670400 bytes, but process.abort() published NOTHING and a V8 heap OOM published NOTHING. The stage that dies that way is build-graph, the exact stage AC-203-GRAPH-B targets, so the exit-event probe cannot discharge the graph criterion. The shipped design therefore publishes a MEASURED figure for every stage that ran and exited normally, and publishes an explicit peakMeasurementUnavailable marker for a stage that RAN and published none, so an unmeasured stage is distinguishable from a stage that never ran. The residual obligation - a MEASURED peak working set for the build-graph stage that aborts with exit 134 - is ROUTED to the owning slice P1-S3-5 and is NOT absorbed here.
evidence: Live full-chain run of npm run rag:update -- --json in this session: build ok 89051136 bytes / 1378 ms, prewarm-embed ok 56520704 bytes / 24077 ms, build-terms ok 254304256 bytes / 100533 ms, build-graph FAILED (exit 134) with NO figure and peakMeasurementUnavailable true / 21935 ms, snapshot and validate CANCELLED with NEITHER a figure NOR the marker. Parent-versus-child measurement: parent maxRSS 43416 KB against a reaped child peak of 8894570496 bytes. Abort-versus-exit measurement: process.exit(3) 45408256 bytes, uncaught throw 45670400 bytes, process.abort() none, V8 heap OOM none. The RED home detector stays INERT: its toPositiveFiniteNumber returns undefined for a boolean and it does not descend into a boolean, so the new marker key cannot be read as a figure.
followup_action: P1-S3-5 owns the build-graph stage and must own a runner-owned sampler or a stage-side report if the AC-203-GRAPH-B measured-peak obligation is to be discharged; the exit-event probe cannot observe a fatal abort. A consumer of the stage reports must compare FULL-RUN figures only (status ok), because a dry-run child publishes a REAL peak figure and only its status separates it.
resolution: open

NOT ONE OF THOSE IS A `P2-S5-3` COMMAND, AND NONE OF THE FOUR COMMANDS THE `P2-S5-3` SLICE PACKET DECLARES (`npm run jest:mjs -- --testPathPatterns="rag-index/__tests__/plan-first-ranking"`, `npm run jest:mjs -- --testPathPatterns="rag-index"`, `npm run jest:mjs -- --testPathPatterns="scripts/mcp-semantic"` AND `node scripts/agent-customization/validate-plan-sync.mjs --plan=plans/cortex-plan-first-retrieval.plans.md`) APPEARS IN THAT LIST. THE REUSABLE RULE: A VALIDATION EXECUTOR THAT RESOLVES ITS TARGET PLAN GLOBALLY IS NOT AN ENFORCEMENT MECHANISM FOR ANY PLAN OTHER THAN THE DEFAULT ONE; THE ALLOW-LIST MUST BE ADDRESSABLE BY `(plan_path, slice_id)` OR THE EXECUTOR MUST REFUSE TO RUN RATHER THAN SILENTLY VALIDATE AGAINST A DIFFERENT PLAN'S COMMAND SET. description: The RAG reindex tools accept exactly ONE repo-relative path per --files= flag. Passing a COMMA-JOINED list (--files=a.ts,b.ts) is NOT a list - the whole string is treated as ONE literal path, the corpus filter matches nothing, and the command prints a zero-document summary while STILL EXITING 0. That is a SILENT NO-OP THAT MIMICS SUCCESS: an agent that trusts the exit code believes the index was refreshed, while the stale documents remain stale and the cortex-index gate stays RED. The correct form is to REPEAT the flag (--files=a.ts --files=b.ts).
evidence: SOURCE ANCHORS (read-only, verified by the 01-planning tracker-amendment instance for fix-packet-P5-S28-law-iteration-1 on 2026-11-21). BEFORE: node rag-index/build-index.mjs --files=examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/browser-entry.ts,examples/neatRacing/host/hud.ts -> output `Semantic index: scanned 0, indexed 0, skipped 0, chunks 0` plus `No matching documents found for: <the comma-joined string>`, EXIT 0 - A SILENT NO-OP THAT LOOKS LIKE SUCCESS. AFTER: node rag-index/build-index.mjs --files=examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/browser-entry.ts --files=examples/neatRacing/host/hud.ts --files=examples/neatRacing/host/hud.departure.ts --files=examples/neatRacing/host/hud.departure.test.ts --files=examples/neatRacing/physics/departure.baseline.test.ts -> `Semantic index: scanned 5, indexed 5, skipped 0, chunks 128`; node rag-index/embed-index.mjs with the SAME repeated flags -> `Embedding build complete: embedded 128, skipped 22223`; node rag-index/validate-index.mjs -> `Semantic index valid: 1853 documents, 22351 chunks`, EXIT 0; the cortex-index gate -> pass TRUE, index_fresh TRUE, every family fresh. THE SOURCE OF TRUTH IS THE TOOL ITSELF: rag-index/build-index.mjs documents `--files=<path>` as a REPEATABLE flag and parses it with parseCliArgs(process.argv.slice(2), { repeatableFlags: [files] }) into an ARRAY; normalizeFiles() then wraps a non-array value into a ONE-element array, so ONE comma-joined string becomes ONE literal path.

description: THE CONSOLIDATED `slice-advancement` GATE PARSES `--changed-files` WITH `.split(',')`, SO A SPACE-SEPARATED LIST IS NOT A LIST - IT BECOMES ONE BOGUS PATH. THE SEVERITY CLASSIFIER THEN SEES A PATH THAT MATCHES NEITHER `src/` NOR `examples/` NOR `benchmarks/`, MISCLASSIFIES THE SLICE AS `TRIVIAL`, AND THE GATE RUNS ONLY 4 OF ITS 7 SUB-GATES - `shared-validation`, `code-coverage` AND `specialist-review` ARE SILENTLY SKIPPED. THE GATE STILL RETURNS `pass: true`, SO AN AGENT THAT TRUSTS THE EXIT CONTRACT BELIEVES IT RAN 7 GATES WHEN IT RAN 4 AND THAT THE COVERAGE, SHARED-VALIDATION AND SPECIALIST-REVIEW LEGS WERE DISCHARGED WHEN THEY NEVER RAN. THIS IS A SILENT COVERAGE HOLE THAT MIMICS SUCCESS - THE SAME CLASS AS THE `--files=` COMMA-JOINED NO-OP IN THE PRECEDING EVENT (learn-20261121-224252-...), WHICH EXPLICITLY ASKED FOR THIS AUDIT IN ITS FOLLOW-UP ITEM (c). THE CORRECT FORM IS COMMA-SEPARATED PATHS (`--changed-files=a,b,c`), WHICH THE GATE'S OWN USAGE BLOCK DOCUMENTS (`--changed-files=f1,f2`) AND WHICH `slice-advancement.gate.mjs:284-287` IMPLEMENTS. THE RULE FOR FUTURE CALLERS: BUILD THE ARGUMENT AS `args: { changed-files: files.join(',') }` AND ASSERT `severity` AND `gateCount` IN THE EVIDENCE ROW, BECAUSE `pass: true` ALONE DOES NOT PROVE THE FULL GATE RAN.
evidence: SOURCE ANCHORS (read-only, verified by the 01-planning VERIFICATION instance for fix-packet-P5-S28-law-iteration-1 on 2026-11-21). THE TOOL: `scripts/agent-customization/gates/slice-advancement.gate.mjs:66-69` READS THE FLAG RAW (`rawArgv.find((a) => a.startsWith('--changed-files='))`), `:284-287` SPLITS IT (`.split(',').map((f) => f.trim()).filter(Boolean)`), `:290` HANDS THE RESULT TO `classifySeverity(changedFiles)`, AND THE GATE'S OWN USAGE BLOCK (`:79` AND `:84`) DOCUMENTS `--changed-files=f1,f2` AS COMMA-SEPARATED. THE CLASSIFIER: `scripts/agent-customization/gates/specialist-review-severity.gate.mjs:87-124` RETURNS `TRIVIAL` WITH `specialistCount: 0` WHEN EVERY CHANGED FILE IS TRIVIAL (TEST / MARKDOWN / FORMATTING / LOCK) AND `FULL` WITH `specialistCount: 1` AS SOON AS ONE FILE TOUCHES RUNTIME LOGIC UNDER `src/`, `examples/` OR `benchmarks/` (`:57`, `:74-77`, `:120-123`). THE REPRODUCTION: THIS PASS RAN THE GATE TWICE WITH A SPACE-SEPARATED SEVEN-FILE SET AND BOTH RUNS RETURNED `pass: true` BUT ONLY `severity: TRIVIAL` AND `gateCount: 4` - THE `shared-validation`, `code-coverage` AND `specialist-review` LEGS NEVER RAN. THE THIRD RUN, WITH THE IDENTICAL SEVEN FILES COMMA-SEPARATED, RETURNED `pass: true`, `severity: FULL`, `gateCount: 7`, `specialistCount: 1`, ALL SEVEN SUB-GATES GREEN (`plan-sync`, `step-packet`, `plan-slice-quality`, `plan-command-lint`, `shared-validation`, `code-coverage`, `specialist-review`), `failedGates: []`, `erroredGates: []`, `timedOutGates: []` - AND THAT VERDICT WAS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE JSON ALREADY ATTACHED TO THE STEP-28 PACKET `evidence.gate_outputs`, WHICH WAS PRODUCED BY THE CORRECT COMMA-SEPARATED FORM. THE GAP IS THEREFORE IN THE CALLER, NOT IN THE GATE'S LOGIC, BUT THE GATE CANNOT DETECT IT BECAUSE A TRUNCATED RUN IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PASSING ONE ON THE SURFACE. THE WORSE CONSEQUENCE: A TRIVIAL-MISCLASSIFIED RUN SKIPS `shared-validation`, WHICH IS THE LEG THAT ACTUALLY RUNS THE TESTS AND THE COVERAGE, SO A SLICE CAN BE REPORTED `pass: true` WITH NO TEST EVER EXECUTED AGAINST ITS CHANGED FILES.

exceptionEvidence.rootCause: TWO LAYERS, AND THE GATE LAYER IS THE ONE THAT MUST BE FIXED. (1) WRITER LAYER: the append that produced the truncated line emitted a PARTIAL JSON string - its final closing brace was never written - so the last physical line of the log was not valid JSON; a writer that never re-reads its own bytes cannot detect this. (2) GATE LAYER: scripts/agent-customization/gates/learning-event.gate.mjs parses every non-empty line inside a try/catch and SWALLOWS the parse error (lines 55-61, comment at line 59: `// Skip malformed lines; presence of valid events is the requirement.`), then asserts only `const pass = events.length > 0;` (line 63). THE GATE THEREFORE REPORTS pass:true AS LONG AS AT LEAST ONE LINE ANYWHERE IN THE 28k-LINE LOG PARSES. A MALFORMED OR TRUNCATED APPENDED EVENT IS THEREFORE INVISIBLE: IT CONTRIBUTES NOTHING TO eventCount, RAISES NO WARNING, PRODUCES NO FAILURE, LEAVES fixHint ON THE PASS-BRANCH STRING, AND THE GATE exitCode STAYS 0. THE ONLY SIGNAL IS THE rawLineCount-vs-eventCount DELTA - 28848 versus 28847 - WHICH THE GATE ALREADY COMPUTES AT LINES 77-78 AND REPORTS IN evidence BUT NEVER ASSERTS ON. NET EFFECT: THE GATE CANNOT DETECT THAT THE NEWEST LINE - THE ONE LINE THAT WAS JUST WRITTEN AND THE ONLY ONE A CALLER CARES ABOUT - IS CORRUPT, AND IT CANNOT DISTINGUISH A HEALTHY 28848-EVENT LOG FROM A 28847-EVENT LOG WITH ONE SILENTLY DROPPED RECORD.

THE REUSABLE RULES FOR APPEND-ONLY EVIDENCE LOGS: (1) THE GATE MUST ASSERT THE rawLineCount-vs-eventCount DELTA: malformedLineCount = rawLineCount - eventCount is EXACTLY the number of unwritten-or-corrupted records, and a non-zero delta is a real defect that must FAIL (or at minimum WARN); (2) THE GATE SHOULD REQUIRE THE LAST NON-EMPTY LINE TO PARSE, because in an append-only log the newest line is the one that matters and the one a truncated writer corrupts; (3) A WRITER MUST ROUND-TRIP ITS OWN OUTPUT - BUILD THE RECORD AS AN OBJECT, SERIALIZE IT WITH JSON.stringify, JSON.parse THE SERIALIZED STRING BACK, AND ONLY THEN APPEND IT WITH A SINGLE TRAILING NEWLINE - A WRITER THAT NEVER RE-READS ITS OWN BYTES CAN EMIT A TRUNCATED LINE AND NEVER KNOW; (4) READ THIS GATE pass:true AS 'THE LOG IS NOT EMPTY', NOT AS 'THE LOG IS WELL-FORMED' - A CALLER THAT NEEDS WELL-FORMEDNESS MUST COMPARE eventCount WITH rawLineCount; (5) A GATE THAT SWALLOWS A PARSE ERROR SHOULD AT LEAST SURFACE THE COUNT OF WHAT IT SWALLOWED - SILENT TOLERATION THAT IS REPORTED BUT NEVER ASSERTED IS THE FALSE-GREEN SHAPE THIS EVENT IS ABOUT.

description: THE `--files=` FLAG ON `rag-index/build-index.mjs` AND `rag-index/embed-index.mjs` IS REPEATABLE ONLY - ONE REPO-RELATIVE PATH PER FLAG. A SINGLE COMMA-JOINED VALUE (E.G. `--files=plans/a.plans.md,plans/b.logs.md`) IS NOT A LIST: THE WHOLE STRING IS CARRIED AS ONE LITERAL PATH, THE CORPUS FILTER MATCHES NO DOCUMENT, NOTHING IS INDEXED, AND BOTH SCRIPTS STILL EXIT 0. THAT IS A SILENT NO-OP THAT MIMICS SUCCESS - A TRACKER CAN CLAIM 'THE INDEX WAS REFRESHED' WHEN IT WAS NOT, AND THE STALE DOCUMENTS REMAIN STALE. THE ONLY CORRECT FORM IS ONE `--files=` FLAG PER PATH: `node rag-index/build-index.mjs --files=plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md --files=plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.logs.md --files=plans/README.md --files=plans/Roadmap.md --json`.

(1) THE PARSER: `rag-index/cli-utils.mjs:29-52` (`parseCliArgs`) TAKES A REPEATABLE FLAG'S VALUE VERBATIM FROM THE `--key=value` TOKEN AND ACCUMULATES REPEATED OCCURRENCES INTO AN ARRAY; IT NEVER SPLITS A VALUE ON COMMAS. THE OPT-IN IS EXPLICIT AT `rag-index/build-index.mjs:600-602` (`parseCliArgs(process.argv.slice(2), { repeatableFlags: ['files'] })`) AND AT `rag-index/embed-index.mjs:683-685` (THE SAME `repeatableFlags: ['files']`). THE TOOLS' OWN HELP STATES THE SEMANTICS: `rag-index/build-index.mjs:13` ('--files=<path> - Repeatable flag that limits indexing to the listed repo-relative paths') AND `:607`/`:614` ('--files=<path>...  Repeatable flag that limits indexing to a repo-relative path'). (2) THE FILTER IS AN EXACT-MATCH MEMBERSHIP TEST, NOT A LIST PARSE: `rag-index/build-index.mjs:60-63` - `const targetFiles = normalizeFiles(options.files); const isTargeted = Array.isArray(targetFiles) && targetFiles.length > 0; const documents = isTargeted ? allDocuments.filter(({ filePath }) => targetFiles.includes(filePath)) : ...`; `normalizeFiles` (`:594-597`) ONLY WRAPS A NON-ARRAY IN A ONE-ELEMENT ARRAY AND DOES NOT SPLIT ON COMMAS, SO A COMMA-JOINED VALUE STAYS ONE STRING AND `includes(filePath)` IS NEVER TRUE FOR ANY DOCUMENT. (4) NET: A COMMA-JOINED CALL INDEXES NOTHING, WARNS, AND EXITS 0 - THE EXIT CODE PROVES NOTHING.
